subject: Bolivia
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Lake Poopó. The pictures are NASA MODIS Terra true colour for 20 March 2014, 2016 and 2017 (GIBS), the same time of year on purpose, because the lake's area varies by season (mean depth under 3 m). They show water and dry bed; the script states only the causes the page lists as suggested.

claims.text: Lake Poopó was a large saline lake in the Altiplano, Bolivia, at an altitude of about 3,700 m, and was the second-largest lake in the country.
The lake had a mean depth of less than 3 m, so its surface area differed greatly seasonally.
At its maximum in 1986 the lake had an area of 3,500 km2.
By December 2015 the lake had completely dried up, leaving only a few marshy areas.
On 20 January 2016 the area was declared a disaster zone by the Bolivian government.
Suggested causes of the decline are the melting of the Andes glaciers, a drought due to climate change, and continued diversion of water for mining and agriculture.
NASA MODIS Terra true-colour pictures of Lake Poopó taken on 20 March 2014, 2016 and 2017 (NASA GIBS).
